sections.h2: Where do I pay property tax in Washington County?
sections.html:
Pay your town, village or city treasurer through January 31, and pay the Washington County Treasurer after that. Wis. Stat. 74.11(6) sends payments made on or before January 31 to the municipal treasurer and every other payment to the county treasurer. That includes the second installment, which is due July 31, and any prior-year delinquent tax.

Look up a parcel on the county's Land Records site by one search term at a time, such as a last name or a street number and name. Open the parcel, scroll to Tax History and select Pay Taxes. Ask the treasurer for office hours and the payoff figure on a specific parcel.

sections.h2: What does it cost to pay Washington County taxes online?
sections.html:
Online payments carry a one-time convenience fee that is added to the amount you owe. The fee goes to Municipal Services Bureau, the company that runs the payment service, and you see the total before you submit.

Payment methodConvenience fee
Credit card2.5 percent of the total due
Debit card$3.50 flat
E-check$1.50

These figures come from the county's Pay Taxes Online page. An e-check is the cheapest route for most bills, and a check mailed early costs nothing.

sections.h2: Does the postmark still protect a mailed Washington County tax payment?
sections.html:
A postmark can still help, but the date on it may be later than the day you mailed. The county treasurer warned residents that since August 2025 the Postal Service applies postmarks at regional sorting centers instead of when an item is first handled. Many tax laws measure a timely payment by the postmark, so an envelope dropped in a mailbox just before January 31 could be stamped several days late.

Under Wis. Stat. 74.11(7), a first installment that is not received by the proper official within five working days after January 31 makes the whole remaining balance delinquent as of February 1. Delinquent real property taxes are paid to the county treasurer with interest and penalties charged from the preceding February 1. The simplest fix is to pay online or mail well ahead of the date. If you are selling, tell your closing agent which installments are already paid.

sections.h2: When do Washington County tax bills arrive?
sections.html:
Bills go out in December. Wis. Stat. 74.09(5) requires each taxing district clerk to mail them no later than the third Monday in December, after the taxing bodies submit their levies by December 1. Under 74.09(6), failing to receive a bill does not change the tax or the collection of delinquent amounts, so contact your municipal clerk if yours has not arrived by the holidays.

If you bought or inherited the home during the year, ask the treasurer to confirm the parcel number and the installments already paid before you send money.

sections.h2: Who sets and reviews assessments in Washington County?
sections.html:
Local assessors set the values, and the board of review in your municipality hears objections. Under Wis. Stat. 70.46, a town board of review is by default the town supervisors and clerk, and a city or village board uses the mayor or president and clerk plus officers the governing body names. The county's Real Property Lister Office handles parcel listing and mapping and acts as the liaison between the county and the Wisconsin Department of Revenue. It is open Monday through Thursday, 7:00 a.m. to 5:30 p.m.

Washington County bills combine levies from several taxing bodies. The bill itself must show the school district tax, the tax from each other taxing jurisdiction and the credits applied, with the change from the prior year, under Wis. Stat. 74.09(3). Compare those lines before you decide whether an appeal is worth your time.

sections.h2: How does a board of review hearing work in Washington County?
sections.html:
The hearing is formal and sworn, and the burden is on the owner. Wis. Stat. 70.47 sets the main requirements:

  • The board meets once a year during a 45-day period starting the fourth Monday of April.
  • Notice of intent to object is due at least 48 hours before the first meeting, with limited waivers for good cause.
  • A written objection goes to the board clerk in the first two hours of the first meeting.
  • The owner must state in writing an estimate of land value and improvement value, with the information used to reach it.
  • The assessor's value is presumed correct unless the owner shows it is wrong.
  • The board votes by roll call, and a tie leaves the assessment in place.

The board can allow an owner to appear by phone or give sworn written statements instead of coming in person. Clerks keep the records for at least seven years, so you can request copies. An owner who refuses a reasonable written request, sent by certified mail, from the assessor to view the exterior of the property loses the right to appear.

sections.h2: How does the lottery and gaming credit work in Washington County?
sections.html:
The credit lowers the tax bill of a Wisconsin resident who owns a dwelling and used it as a primary residence on January 1 of the levy year. You must apply, because it is not automatic. File with the county treasurer where the property is located, or with the city treasurer if the city collects taxes under Wis. Stat. 74.87.

If the credit is missing from your bill, apply to the town, village or city treasurer by January 31 after you receive the bill. A late claim goes to the Department of Revenue by October 1 after the bill is issued. You can claim only one primary residence, and the county says these do not qualify:

  • Rental units
  • Vacant land
  • Garages
  • Business property

A person temporarily away for about six months or less, for example in a hospital, still has the home they return to as their residence.

sections.h2: What does Washington County look like to a seller?
sections.html:
Washington County is the fifth-smallest county in Wisconsin by area, at 436 square miles, and it sits in the Milwaukee metro area north of Waukesha County. The 2020 census counted 136,761 residents and 58,311 housing units, with a 4.2 percent vacancy rate. Of the occupied homes, 77.3 percent were owner-occupied.

West Bend is the county seat. Hartford is the other city of any size, and the villages include Germantown, Jackson, Kewaskum, Newburg, Richfield and Slinger. Schools include Germantown, Kewaskum, Slinger and Hartford Union high schools, and the county contains part of the Kettle Moraine State Forest.

Commuting is a point buyers raise. The county ended its Commuter Express service at the end of 2023, so there is no public transit link from Washington County to the rest of the Milwaukee metro area, though shared ride taxi service remains. For an inherited or tenant-occupied house, ask the county treasurer for the tax history on the parcel before you set a closing date.

faqs.q: When are Washington County property taxes due?
faqs.a: January 31 is the deadline for the first installment or full payment, and July 31 is the deadline for the second installment. Pay the municipal treasurer through January 31 and the county treasurer after that.

faqs.q: How much does it cost to pay Washington County taxes by card?
faqs.a: Credit cards add a 2.5 percent fee, debit cards add $3.50 and e-checks add $1.50. The fee is added on top of the tax owed, and you see the total before you submit.

faqs.q: Will a mailed payment count if I mail it on January 30?
faqs.a: It may not. Since August 2025 the Postal Service applies postmarks at regional sorting centers, so an envelope can be postmarked days after you mail it. The county treasurer suggests paying online or mailing earlier.

faqs.q: Who qualifies for the lottery and gaming credit in Washington County?
faqs.a: A Wisconsin resident who owns a home and uses it as a primary residence on January 1 of the levy year qualifies. You must apply, and rentals, vacant land and garages do not qualify.

faqs.q: How do I appeal my Washington County assessment?
faqs.a: Give notice to your municipal board of review at least 48 hours before its first meeting and file a written objection in the first two hours of that meeting. The board meets during a 45-day window that begins on the fourth Monday of April.
